m3-324: Item 6 of Schedule 3 charges $945 for each person in relation to whom the application is made, so an application naming two directors pays $1,890; 'for each application' changes the unit of charge and is false under bank/FORMAT.md. The statement is the existing one and was not changed by this batch.
m1-227: Section 12(2) is the general rule for CBNIs imported or exported as cargo (Division 2 of Part 3); the fall-backs in s.12(3)–(4) apply only when no reference exchange rate is published on the reference day, which the statement neither asserts nor denies.
m3-350: Section 18(1)(a) makes the intermediary's written consent a necessary condition; the statement says the institution may use the intermediary only if the consent is given, and does not claim that consent is the sole condition (the s.18(1)(b) undertaking is tested by the next statement).
m3-352: Section 9(1)(a) speaks of documents, data or information 'referred to in section 2(1)(a) or (ab)' not previously used for verification under that section; the statement's 'under Schedule 2' names the same verification regime without widening it, and the deciding quote carries the full wording.
m6-513: ¶10.10 covers batch files from a single originator to overseas recipients, where the batch file must still carry complete and accurate originator and recipient information; it is not an option to omit that information. The statement concerns the ¶10.11 option, which the paragraph confines to domestic wire transfers, and the explanation now says so.
m4-416: The statement follows the cited Licensing Guide ¶6.2 word for word (within 30 days upon receipt of the invitation letter); the Guidance Notes ¶4.6 count from the issue of the reminder letter, which ruling B23 records as a source difference, not a defect in this statement.
